summary: Eggers was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tartu under Leo Meyer and Leopold von Schroeder. He later served at Tallinn Cathedral School (1896-1914), Privatlyzeum Greifswald (1919-1928), and Zemkessches Privatlyzeum (1928).
Faulkner worked in Indology and other fields. He served in the Indian Civil Service starting in 1839 and was an Assistant Commissioner in the Customs, Salt, and Opium Department until 1874.
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy from around 1903 to 1907 and under Christian Bartholomae around 1906 to 1907.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gardner studied at Kalamazoo College, Michigan State University, and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. 2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., Robert H. Sharf, and Janet Gyatso. He later joined the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Hamilton was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu Literature at the East India Company College (1806-1818). In 1823, he founded the Royal Asiatic Society and taught scholars including Franz Bopp and Friedrich Schlegel.
Diack was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Aberdeen from 1876 to 1879 and at King's College, Cambridge, from 1879 to 1881.
Working in Buddhist studies and Japanology, O'Neill became a PhD candidate at the University of Toronto and held an appointment as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Johnston, an Indologist and historian, studied law at the University of Göttingen and Lincoln's Inn. He served on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811-1819), became Chief Justice, and founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1823.

Working in Japanology and Buddhist studies, Kabanoff was attested in 2000 as a Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Kazembek worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1826-1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1849-1870).

Smith specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at American University, Oxford, and EPHE (Ph.D. 2016), he held posts at EPHE, Otani University, University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, Armchair Academics (2021), and Ligature Historical Filmwerke (2025).

An Indologist and historian, Forbes studied at the East India Company College and under Dalpatram (~1848-1865). He founded the Gujarat Vernacular Society (1848) and Forbes Gujarati Sabha (1865), and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1862).

Lubotsky, a specialist in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University (Ph.D. under Robert S. P. Beekes). In 1999, he became professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden University.
Macmillan, active in religious and Buddhist studies, studied at SIT Graduate Institute under advisor Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).

Broadley was an Indology and history scholar who studied law at Lincoln's Inn from around 1866 to 1869. He subsequently served in the Indian Civil Service as an Assistant and Collector between 1869 and 1872.
Murray was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned his D.D. at the University of Edinburgh (~1794-1812) and was appointed its Professor of Oriental Languages in 1812.

Hsu specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer (~2011-2018) and later held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.

Piatigorsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying at Moscow State University. He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957-1968), University of Oxford (~1974-1975), and SOAS University of London (lecturer 1975, professor 1990-2001).

Potebnja was a linguist and philosopher who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Kharkiv, also studying under Albrecht Weber. He spent his career at Kharkiv as a professor from 1875, and joined the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences in 1875.

Rea was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India, starting as an Assistant in 1882, becoming its head in 1886, and serving as Superintendent from 1902 to 1913.
